description: yagami is a self-hosted gateway that exposes the coding-agent CLIs already installed and signed in on a machine (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, and any ACP agent) as an Anthropic- and OpenAI-compatible API. It also ships a zero-config library so local apps can drive those CLIs without URLs or API keys. Intended for personal use only.
features: Serves Anthropic /v1/messages and OpenAI /v1/chat/completions with one API key
Drives signed-in Claude Code via the Agent SDK, no separate vendor keys
Drives Codex via codex exec and ACP-registry agents via Agent Client Protocol
Zero-config Yagami library client mirroring Anthropic and OpenAI SDK surfaces
Library syncs with the host's yagami config file and environment variables
Anthropic server tools web_search and web_fetch run inside the engine
MCP connector: mcp_servers and mcp_toolset connect tools for a single turn
Streaming SSE responses synthesized in both Anthropic and OpenAI dialects
Full agentic Claude Code sessions embeddable for building UIs
Session cache maps conversation prefixes to Claude Code session ids for resume
Detects installed and signed-in CLIs and reports harness status
Settings parity modes: terminal, project, or isolated config loading
Reports agent error reasons and usage-limit errors to callers

run: make — bun install, build, and link yagami into ~/.local/bin

bun run dev — run the CLI from source with tsx

bun run smoke / live:providers / live:session / live:harnesses — script checks in scripts/
conventions: Package manager is bun; the Makefile runs bun install and bun run build
prepublishOnly must pass typecheck and test before publish
Keep the endpoint private and do not share API keys (README)

cli.summary: This layer is the `yagami` command-line tool and the package's build and public entry points. Commander defines the commands (start, stop, status, key, and daemon mode) in src/cli.ts, which starts the HTTP server through the server layer. tsup bundles the entries into ESM under dist/, and src/index.ts defines the library surface. Before changing anything here, know that the CLI is a thin wrapper that drives the server layer, and that the public API is whatever src/index.ts exports.

map.name: CLI commands: start, stop, status, key, daemon mode
Public library exports (what the package exposes)
Build output and bundle entries (dist/cli.js, index, server, type declarations)
End-to-end smoke test against the real Claude Code CLI

flows.name: Starting the server from the CLI
steps: Commander parses the start flags (port, host, claude path, provider) in src/cli.ts
The CLI loads the saved config and the config file through server/config.js
The CLI calls startYagami from the server layer
The running server's state is written to the state file via writeServerState
Later status and stop calls read that state and check whether the recorded process is alive

flows.name: Building the package
steps: tsup reads tsup.config.ts
It bundles three ESM entries: index, server, and cli
It targets node20 with sourcemaps
Type declarations are emitted for index and server only
clean: true clears dist/ before writing dist/cli.js

flows.name: Smoke test
steps: scripts/smoke.ts starts the server on a random local port with a throwaway key
It sends a non-streaming request to /v1/messages through the real Claude Code CLI
It checks the response status and text
It exits with code 1 on failure
It is run manually because it spends real tokens

files: src/cli.ts — the commander commands and daemon handling for the yagami binary
src/index.ts — the library entry: re-exports the client, harness listing, and Anthropic/OpenAI helpers
tsup.config.ts — bundle entries, format, target, and declaration setup
src/version.ts — the VERSION constant shown by the CLI
scripts/smoke.ts — manual end-to-end check of a real completion
rules: Smoke test costs real tokens against the signed-in Claude Code CLI; run it only by hand
Declarations are emitted only for index and server, so cli has no .d.ts output
clean: true in tsup wipes dist/ on every build
Anything exported from src/index.ts is public API; changing an export changes what library users get
Server mode is reached through the server entry (yagami/server), not the library index
src/cli.ts keeps the node shebang; the built dist/cli.js is the executable

Engine — smoke.ts reads the running server's engine.claudePath; index.ts re-exports the engine
Library client — index.ts re-exports the Yagami client, harness listing, and session types

Diagnostics — cli.ts reports through the debug function in core/log
Node runtime — the bundle targets node20 and runs as an ESM Node program

providers.summary: The provider adapters layer turns a Provider interface into concrete runners for each harness: the Claude Agent SDK, `codex exec` and `codex app-server`, ACP agents, and generic print or JSONL process CLIs. Each adapter yields the same TurnEvent stream, and capabilities declare what each can natively honor. A newcomer must grasp that the engine emulates or rejects whatever a provider's capabilities do not declare, and that child processes are ended as whole trees, not single PIDs.

map.name: Permission and elicitation prompts from a harness

flows.name: A completion turn through a process provider
steps: The engine calls the provider's turn method with a TurnRequest
The adapter resolves its CLI binary via executable.ts (explicit path, PATH, then common install dirs)
The adapter spawns the CLI with its non-interactive arguments, writing the prompt to stdin when there is no {prompt} placeholder
Output is read line by line (readline, or JSONL for jsonl.ts) and mapped to TurnEvent values such as session, thinking, text and done
Failures are classified in errors.ts into ProviderError, UsageLimitError or AuthRequiredError
When the turn ends, killTree in process.ts ends the whole process tree

flows.name: A harness asks for permission or input mid-turn
steps: The adapter receives a tool-permission request or an elicitation from the CLI
permission.ts or interaction.ts converts it into the host-facing request type
The host handler returns a decision
The adapter translates the decision back into the CLI's protocol reply
If no handler is set, a handler throws, or the request is aborted, the configured default decision is used

src/core/providers/jsonl.ts — the generic JSONL process runner

rules: Every provider must declare its capabilities honestly; the engine emulates or rejects anything not declared
Ending a CLI must go through killTree, never a bare child.kill(), because launchers and MCP servers can outlive the top process
A prompt written as a CLI argument can be read as a flag or exceed the argument limit, so prefer stdin when the args have no {prompt} placeholder
Failures must be classified in errors.ts so the engine maps them to the right API error
Permission and elicitation decisions must be translated through permission.ts and interaction.ts, not ad hoc
Caught errors in this layer are reported through log.ts, not silently dropped
edges: Engine — the engine calls each provider's turn and session methods and maps TurnEvent values into SSE and responses
Engine — reads ProviderCapabilities to decide what to emulate or reject
Library client — session wrappers and harness listing use the same provider and session types
Diagnostics — debug() from log.ts reports swallowed failures
Wire contract — the typed TurnRequest and TurnEvent shapes in provider.ts and types.ts
Node runtime — spawns the Claude Code, Codex and ACP CLIs installed on the host
